_comment: The evaluation set. Delete this first entry and replace the rest with your own.
Each case needs a projectId, a question, and what SHOULD come back — either
expectedPages (combined page numbers, which you can read off the viewer) or
expectedChunkIds if you have them. A case passes when any expected page or
chunk appears in the retrieved list.
Build it with: node benchmarks/retrieval_eval.mjs --capture "your question" --project <id>
which runs the question and prints the top hits with their page numbers, so
you mark up what is actually right rather than typing ids by hand.
Aim for 30-50 cases, and TAG them by class. The tag breakdown is the useful
part: an average hides that identifier lookups went from 40% to 95% while
open questions went slightly backwards, and that is exactly the trade a
retrieval change makes. The four classes below are the ones that behave
differently in this app; keep roughly ten of each.
Include failures you have actually seen. A set of questions you already know

question: what is S102A
note: Sheet lookup by number — the case dense embeddings cannot resolve, since S102A and S201 are equally 'a structural sheet number'.

question: where is detail A-301 referenced
note: Detail tag with a separator — the shape Postgres FTS mangles into '-301'.

question: what size are the W18x97 beams
note: Member designation. Fails on dense alone for the same reason sheet numbers do.

question: what is the live load on the truss lines
note: A number stated in a general note. Dense usually finds this; keep it in the set so a change that breaks it is visible.

question: what holds up the canopy
note: Shares no vocabulary with the note that answers it — the case keyword search cannot do, and the reason dense retrieval stays in the mix.
